statements.text: P1: two realizations $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the same complete present local state ($X^\alpha_t = X^\beta_t$) and the same inputs ($I^\alpha = I^\beta$) can still be assigned different consciousness, $f(X^\alpha_t, X^\alpha_{<t}) \neq f(X^\beta_t, X^\beta_{<t})$, because their prior histories differ. A process theory must hold this, or its attribution is merely state-based.

sources.quote: A process theory must be irreducibly history-dependent. The requirement of differential attribution (16) must persist even when the complete present local state and inputs are made equal between the two realizations.
